(By Sri.K.Pujar,Adv)
 :Judgment:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioners against Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- for the death of Rudresha S/o Ramanna in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 01.04.2023 at about 01.25 p.m., when Rudresha was riding his motor cycle bearing No.KA-01-EC-3723 on Bangalore-Tumkur NH-48 Service Road, near Sugganahalli Village, Yadavani-Huliyur Durga main road, Kunigal Taluk, Tumkur, at that time, one car bearing Reg.No.KA-15-A-3003 came from same direction in rash and negligent manner and hit the motor cycle from back side.

Due to the impact,
Rudresha fell down and sustained grievous head injury.

On the way to the hospital,
he succumbed to the said injuries.
Prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and he was doing agriculture work and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
The Petitioners were entirely depending upon the income of the deceased.
Due to the death of Rudresha, the Petitioners have lost their bread earner.
The Respondent No.1 is the RC owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending car and therefore, the Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
3. In pursuance of service of notice, the Respondents appeared before the Court through their respective Counsels.
But respondent No.1 has not filed objections to the main petition.
The respondent No.2 filed objections to the main petition.

Respondent No.2 in the written statement denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased Rudresha and it also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.
Further, it admits the issuance of insurance policy to the car bearing Reg.No.KA-15-A-3003.

Further it contended that the rider of the motor cycle was not having valid and effective driving licence and the accident took place due to his negligence and also contended that the deceased was not wearing helmet.
Further it contended that the driver of car was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.

Further contended that the petition is liable to be dismissed for non joinder of necessary parties i.e, owner and insurer of motor Chikkamma vs Shivashankara R on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48595772/
2 cycle.
On these grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival pleadings, my Learned Predecessor has framed the following Issues.:
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal representative of the deceased?

2. Whether the Petitioners prove that Rudresha.
S/o Ramanna died due to injuries sustained by him in an accident occurred on 01.04.2023 at about 01.25 p.m. near Sugganahalli Village, Yadavani-Huliyur Durga main road, Kunigal Taluk, Tumkur,
Karnataka arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of car bearing No.KA-15-A-3003?
3. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

4. What Order or Award?
5. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, the Petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 13 documents as per Ex.P.1 to 13 and closed her side evidence.

On the other hand,
Respondents have not adduced any evidence.

6. Having heard both side and perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No. 3 : Partly in the Affirmative.
 Issue No. 4 : As per the Final Order  for the following :
 REASONS  7. Issue No.2:
This issue is taken at first instance for discussion.

It is the case of the Petitioners that the son of Petitioner No.1 by name Rudresha was died in the Road traffic accident that occurred on 01.04.2023.
8.
On the other hand, the Respondents have denied the said accident occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.

sentences.text: In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, Petitioner No.1 got examined herself as P.W.1 and she has filed her chief affidavit in lieu of chief examination and re-iterated the petition averments.
10. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, PW1 has relied on Ex.P-1 to Ex.P13.
Ex. P-1

and 2 are the True copies of FIR and complaint which show that the Huliyurdurga Police have registered the case against the driver of the offending car for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 304(A)
of IPC.
Ex.P3 and 4 are the Spot Panchanama and sketch, which show that the concerned police had drawn Mahazar and prepared the sketch at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P.5 is the Inquest.
Ex.P.6 is the copy of PM report which shows the cause of death is due to " Head injury sustained".
Ex.P.7 is the IMV report which shows that accident did not occur due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles.

Ex.P.8 is the true copy of the Charge-sheet which shows that the I.O of Huliyurdurga Police station has submitted Charge-sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 304(A) of IPC.
11.
Exs.P.9 and 10 are the Aadhar cards of Petitioners No.1 and 2.

Ex.P.11 is copy of ration card,
which shows the name and age of deceased.

Ex.P.12 and 13 are the copies of RTC extract pertaining to the land belongs to petitioner No.2.
12. PW1 is subjected for cross examination by the learned counsel for Respondent No.2.

During her cross examination she has denied all the suggestions made by the counsel for respondent No.2.
13.
The respondents have not adduced any evidence to rebut the evidence of petitioners.
14. Moreover, the charge sheet is the material document, which is not challenged by the driver of the offending vehicle.

Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence adduced by the Petitioner No.1 and the documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the Petitioners have proved that the said accident has occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Car bearing No.KA-15-A-3003 and in the said accident, the son of PW1 had sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 is in the "Affirmative".

Issue No. 1 and 3:
15.
Both these issues are taken together for common discussion as they are interlinked with each other and to avoid the repetition of the facts.
16. It is stated in the Petition that the Petitioner No.1 is the mother of the deceased and Petitioner No.2 is the father of the deceased Rudresha.
In order to prove this fact, PW.1 has produced her Aadhar Card and the Aadhar card of the petitioner No. 2 and ration card of their family at Ex.P.11.
Upon going through the same, it clearly shows the relationship of the deceased with the petitioners.
Hence, the petitioners have proved that they are the legal heirs of the deceased Rudresha.
17. In the petition, the age of the deceased was shown as 33 years and his avocation is shown as agriculture and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.

PW.1 has produced RTC extract to prove the Chikkamma vs Shivashankara R on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48595772/
4 occupation of deceased.
But the said RTCs are standing in the name of petitioner No.2.
Though these documents prove that the family of petitioner has landed properties and they are the agriculturists.
But, there is no document to prove the income of the deceased.

In the absence of any other documentary evidence before the Court to prove the income of the deceased, it is proper to take the notional income of the deceased Rudresha as Rs.16,000/- as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, as the said accident has been occurred in the year 2023.
18.
Further, the Petitioners stated the age of the deceased Rudresha as 33 years at the time of the accident.
PW.1 has produced ration card of their family at Ex.P.11, which shows that deceased was 12 years as on 28.05.2009.
The alleged accident was occurred on 01.04.2023.
That means, as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased Rudresha was 26 years.
But in the FIR his age is shown as 30 years and in the inquest Panchnama and PM report shown as 31 years.
Therefore, there is no authenticated document to show the age of deceased.
Hence it is proper to consider the age of deceased shown in the petition as 33 years.
19. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioners are entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF CONSORTIUM, COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF ESTATE, COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUNERAL EXPENSES:
20.
The deceased has left behind him, his mother and father.
Hence, the Petitioner No.1 and 2 are considered as dependents.

At this juncture, I would like to go through principles laid down in the decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that : "Loss of estate has to be compensated by awarding Rupees 14,500/-, loss of consortium should be Rupees 40,000/- and funeral expenses should be Rupees 15,000/-".

entities.text: Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The aforesaid amounts should be enhanced @ 10% in every three years."

As this Court has already observed that the Petitioner No.1 is the mother and Petitioner is the father of the deceased Rudresha, the Petitioners are entitled for a sum of Rupees 44,000/- each towards loss of consortium and Rupees 16,500/- towards loss of estate and Rupees 16,500/- towards funeral expenses.
IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF LOVE AND AFFECTION,
21.
Petitioner No.1 is the mother and she lost her son's love and care and Petitioner No.2 is the son of deceased Rudresha and he lost his father's love and care in their old age.
Bearing in mind the relationship of the Petitioners with the deceased, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS TRANSPORTATION OF DEAD BODY:

5 22.

sentences.text: The accident has occurred near Sugganahalli village, Kunigal Taluk and postmortem was done at Government Hospital at Kunigal Town and obviously body would be buried in his village at Thore Bommanahalli, Kunigal Taluk.
Hence, the Petitioners might have spent some amount towards transportation of body of the deceased.
Hence, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.10,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

VI. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF DEPENDANCY:
23.
It is pertinent to note here that as per the detailed discussion as made supra, the income of the deceased was taken at Rs.16,000/- p.m.

At this juncture, I would like to go through the decision reported in :
1) 2018 ACJ 740, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India At New Delhi in between Manuswamy and others V/s.
Managing Director, Tamil Nadu State Trans. Corpn. Ltd, wherein it is held as under:
"Quantum fatal accident Principle of assessment Future prospects Deceased aged :
21, contract worker in a company - High Court did not consider future prospects while computing compensation - Whether claimants are entitled to compensation after addition of 40 per cent of income of the deceased towards future prospects "
- Held : - yes.
2) 2018 ACJ 5, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, at New Delhi in between Hem Raj Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., and others wherein it is held as under :
"Quantum Fatal accident - Principles of assessment Future prospects Deceased aged 40 Upholding objections of insurance company that principle of addition on account of future prospects is not applicable where income of the deceased is determined by guesswork

6

The decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that: "In case self employed or person on fixed salary the addition should be 40% below the age of 40 years".

entities.text: Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this Petition, the deceased was aged 33 years at the time of accident.
Hence, towards future prospects 40% of the income has to be added.
So, 40% of Rs.16,000/- comes to Rs.6,400/-.
Therefore, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.22,400/- p.m. (Rs.16,000/- + Rs.6400/-).
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 16.

entities.text: (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Sarla Verma's case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held that if the deceased was bachelor Half (1/2) of the income of the deceased may be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

After deducting Half (  ) towards his personal expenses in Rs.22,400/- it comes to Rs.11,200/-
(22,400 - 11,200/-) and multiplier applied is 16 which comes to Rs.21,50,400/- (11,200X 12 X 16 =
Rs.21,50,400/-).
Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.21,50,400/- towards loss of dependency.

24. TOTAL QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONERS ARE ENTITLED:
1. Loss of consortium Rs. 88,000/-
2. Loss of Love and Affection Rs. 50,000/-
3. Loss of Estate Rs. 16,500/-
4. Funeral Expenses Rs. 16,500/-
5. Expenses of transportation Rs. 10,000/-
of dead body 6. Loss of Dependency Rs.21,50,400/-
Total Rs.23,31,400/-
Thus, totally the Petitioners are awarded compensation of Rs.23,31,400/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.
25. Regarding Liability :
As already discussed in the Issue No.2, in this case the driver of the offending Car bearing Reg.No.KA-15-A-3003 was charge-sheeted.
Further, there is no dispute about the validity of the Insurance Policy of the offending vehicle as on the date of accident.

Therefore,
Respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 being the insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
Accordingly, I answer Issue Chikkamma vs Shivashankara R on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48595772/

7 No.2 is in the "Affirmative" and Issue No.3 "Partly in the Affirmative".
26. Issue No.4 :
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.23,31,400/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.23,31,400/- along with costs and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
However, Respondent No.2 being the  insurer is directed to deposit the  compensation amount as stated supra with interest at the rate of 6% p.a within 60 days from the date of this award.

Compensation amount awarded to the Petitioners are apportioned among them are as shown below:
1) 55% to the Petitioner No.1.
2) 45% to the Petitioner No.2 After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 and 2,
75% each of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.1 and 2 respectively by way of E-payment after their proper identification and the remaining 25% each of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner No.1 and 2 respectively in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of their choice.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.

However, Respondent No.2 being the  insurer is directed to deposit the  compensation amount as stated supra with interest at the rate of 6% p.a within 60 days from the date of this award.

Compensation amount awarded to the Petitioners are apportioned among them are as shown below:
1) 55% to the Petitioner No.1.
2) 45% to the Petitioner No.2 After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 and 2,
75% each of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.1 and 2 respectively by way of E-payment after their proper identification and the remaining 25% each of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner No.1 and 2 respectively in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of their choice.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
